display: Second-generation laksa hawker at a Toa Payoh hawker centre. My father started the stall in 1978, and I still pound the rempah by hand.

signals.text: The stall rent went up at the last tender and I'm absorbing it without raising the $4.50 bowl price for the older regulars.
Ingredient costs, especially cockles, keep rising. I'm quietly trimming portions and would like a smarter way to manage this.
I sell about 180 bowls on a weekday. Rent and costs mean I need roughly thirty more bowls a month just to stay level.
My daughter wants to study French cuisine overseas, and I don't understand how culinary school applications, portfolios or reference letters work.
I'd like to find a way for my daughter to fund culinary school abroad, but I don't know what scholarships or funding routes exist.
I'm looking for someone patient who could learn to hand-pound the rempah the way my father taught me, because I can't do all the physical prep alone forever.
I'm worried that nobody will carry on the family recipe in the same way, and I have only written it down in an exercise book.
I'm not comfortable with online forms and English-language portals, so anything with paperwork or applications stalls with me.
I'm tired by the end of long stall days, and I've been getting less rest than I need.
Other hawkers around me are anxious about the rents and some talk of leaving, but nobody has a plan.
I sometimes feel proud when visitors ask about the ingredients, and I wonder if there is a better way to tell the story of this laksa.
I find it hard to ask for help, so I mostly keep problems to myself.

offers.text: A family laksa made with a hand-pounded rempah, a recipe my father started in 1978 and I have run since 1999, at a Toa Payoh hawker centre.
Nearly 50 years of hawker-stall know-how: running a stall, queue handling, and keeping quality up at roughly 180 bowls a day.
Can teach the technique of hand-pounding rempah, and explain why each ingredient is used, to someone who is serious about learning it.
Long relationships with suppliers of cockles, tau pok and fish cake, and can make introductions for people who want to source well.
A stone mortar and pestle from 1980 and a family recipe, which can be part of a food story, a documentary or a tasting session.
Handwritten accounts covering decades of small-stall costs and prices, which can show what has changed for hawkers.
Can explain on the ground what the tender and rent increases mean for a stall's daily sums.
A regular crowd of about 40 customers and a steady daily flow of people, who can be reached through the stall for a small food or community project.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I run admissions support for a culinary school and I'd like to explain portfolios, reference letters and fees to a young cook's family in plain language.
catchers.can: I can bring my daughter Mei, who is 23 and polytechnic-trained, to talk to you, and I can attend an open day with her.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to explain the application process in plain language and in person, rather than only through an online portal?

catchers.hypo: I'm a chef who trained in France and I can mentor young Singaporean cooks who want to study in Lyon.
catchers.can: Through my daughter Mei, who wants to learn French cuisine, I can arrange an introduction and a conversation.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally trained or worked in a French culinary school or kitchen?

catchers.hypo: I know of scholarships and grants for young Singaporeans studying culinary arts abroad and can walk a family through the forms.
catchers.can: I can pass this on to my daughter Mei, who has already said she will apply, and sit with her through the first meeting.
catchers.confirm: Do the scholarships you know of cover culinary school tuition for students from Singapore?

catchers.hypo: I'm making a film or book about disappearing hawker recipes and I want to record a family laksa being made from scratch.
catchers.can: I can show the full hand-pounded rempah process at the stall and share the story of the 1978 stall, within the hours I can spare.
catchers.confirm: Can you work around a stall that can't close for more than a day and a Monday-morning pounding schedule?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young cook who wants to apprentice in a traditional hawker stall and learn the whole process, not just the cooking.
catchers.can: I can teach the rempah pounding and the recipe steps, and see whether you are a good fit to carry the recipe on.
catchers.confirm: Are you willing to commit to early mornings and long hours at a stall for at least a few months?

catchers.hypo: I'm helping a group of hawkers understand tender rent increases and want to hear from stallholders about what it does to their daily sums.
catchers.can: I can share my own experience, and I can put you in touch with neighbouring stallholders such as Auntie Pat, who has the same worries.
catchers.confirm: Are you working with hawkers at an actual hawker centre, rather than studying them from a distance?

catchers.hypo: I run a small food supplier and I want to find a reliable, fairly priced source of cockles or tau pok for hawkers.
catchers.can: I can compare notes from my own suppliers and tell you what has changed in prices and supply.
catchers.confirm: Do you supply to small hawker stalls in Singapore at volumes of a few kilograms a day?

catchers.hypo: My own parent runs a hawker stall and none of us want to take it over. How do families handle the handover of a recipe?
catchers.can: I can talk honestly about how I took over from my father, and about my own worries about what happens next. A fellow hawker I know has a child who doesn't want to take over, and I can suggest we talk.
catchers.confirm: Is your family stall still running, and are you looking for ways to hand it over rather than close it?

forbids.text: I can't leave the stall for more than a day, so I can't travel or take long off-site commitments.
I can't do very long physical work in one stretch, so work with me has to be at a pace a stallholder can manage.
I'm not comfortable with online forms and English-language portals, so I need help or an in-person walk-through for any paperwork.
I won't change the recipe or the hand-pounded rempah method for the sake of speed or branding.
I won't raise prices on my older regulars just to cover rent.
I won't share medical details or exact savings figures with anyone.

projects.name: Mei's culinary school path
projects.text: My daughter wants to study French cuisine overseas, in Lyon or via a Singapore route, and the family needs help understanding applications, funding and what to prepare.
roles_needed: culinary school alumni or chef mentor
someone to help with English-language applications

projects.name: Passing on the laksa
projects.text: A way to keep the family laksa and the hand-pounded rempah going after me, by finding someone to learn it, and by recording the method properly.

policy.t1: When there is a real sign of cooperation I'll talk about the rent increase, my daily volume, my daughter's plans in general terms, and what I can teach or introduce.
policy.t2: When the match looks strong and I know who you are, I'll talk about my worries over savings, tuition and applications, and what happens to the recipe.
policy.never: Medical details and exact savings figures.
